node.name: tsconfig.tsbuidinfo
node.rich_text:
## What is `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`?
It's a **TypeScript compiler cache file** — automatically generated by TypeScript to make rebuilds faster. You never create or edit it.
---
### Why it exists:
When `tsconfig.json` has `"incremental": true` (yours does), TypeScript saves a snapshot of its last compilation:
``` First build: TypeScript checks ALL files → saves cache → tsbuildinfo created Second build: TypeScript reads cache → only checks CHANGED files → much faster ```
---
### Simple analogy:
``` tsbuildinfo = TypeScript's memory
Without it: "Let me re-read all 500 files again..." (slow) With it: "Only 2 files changed, I'll check those" (fast) ```
---
### Key facts:
| Fact | Detail | |---|---| | **Auto-generated?** | Yes — by TypeScript compiler | | **Edit it?** | Never | | **In `.gitignore`?** | Yes — `*.tsbuildinfo` is ignored | | **Safe to delete?** | Yes — TypeScript recreates it next build | | **Contents** | JSON with file hashes and type info |
---
### If you ever have weird TypeScript errors, delete it:
```bash rm frontend/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo npm run dev # TypeScript does a fresh full check ```
This fixes "ghost errors" where TypeScript complains about something that looks correct.
---
### Summary:
``` tsconfig.tsbuildinfo = TypeScript's speed cache auto-generated, never committed, never edited safe to delete if TypeScript behaves strangely ```
It's one of the most boring files in the project — it just silently makes `npm run dev` start faster.
